research_question: In adolescents and adults with asthma that remains uncontrolled on medium-dose inhaled corticosteroids (ICS), do randomised controlled trials show that adding a long-acting beta2 agonist (LABA) to the same medium-dose ICS in a single inhaler reduces the risk of experiencing at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation during the full treatment period compared with the same medium-dose ICS alone?
treatment_label: Medium-dose ICS plus LABA in one inhaler
control_label: The same medium-dose ICS alone at the same dose
outcome_description: Dichotomous participant-level outcome: number of randomised or analysed participants with at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation during the full treatment period, divided by the corresponding number of participants in each eligible arm. Moderate or severe exacerbations are those requiring systemic corticosteroids, an emergency visit, or hospitalisation. Prefer the reported definition closest to combined moderate-or-severe exacerbations; if unavailable, use severe exacerbations alone. Use participant counts rather than exacerbation rates and intention-to-treat data when available.
positive_direction: For sign-harmonised continuous effects, a positive Hedges g would mean fewer moderate or severe exacerbations and therefore favour medium-dose ICS/LABA; for the prespecified Risk Ratio, RR values below 1 favour medium-dose ICS/LABA and values above 1 favour ICS alone.
search_queries: asthma medium dose inhaled corticosteroid LABA randomized controlled trial exacerbation
ICS LABA versus ICS alone asthma trial participant exacerbation
fluticasone salmeterol budesonide formoterol randomized asthma exacerbation controlled
inclusion_criteria: Randomised trials enrolling adolescents and/or adults with asthma that is uncontrolled on medium-dose ICS, without restriction by LABA or ICS brand, dosing schedule, trial duration, or sample size.

Trials comparing a single-inhaler medium-dose ICS/LABA regimen with the same ICS alone at the same medium dose; in multi-arm trials, only these eligible arms are included and a shared control arm retains its full reported sample size and event count.

Trials reporting, or allowing extraction of, quantitative participant-level counts for at least one moderate or severe exacerbation over the full treatment period, using the number randomised or analysed as reported and intention-to-treat data when available.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomised trial, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, protocols, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.

No eligible comparison between medium-dose ICS/LABA in one inhaler and the same medium-dose ICS-alone control at the same dose; this includes studies with only high-dose ICS, high-dose ICS/LABA, ICS plus LAMA, or other comparators.

No quantitative participant-level outcome data capable of producing the requested effect size: no arm-level numbers of participants with at least one eligible exacerbation and denominators (or equivalent extractable proportions); exacerbation rates per person-year alone are insufficient, although participant counts reported elsewhere in the paper are eligible.
Completely unrelated to adolescents or adults with uncontrolled asthma treated with medium-dose ICS-based regimens.
moderators_to_extract: ICS/LABA drug combination and component brands
ICS and LABA dose schedule or dosing frequency
Population age group (adolescents, adults, or mixed)
Exacerbation definition used (moderate-or-severe combined versus severe only)
Baseline asthma severity or prior exacerbation history
effect_size_note: Pool arm-level participant counts as Risk Ratios comparing medium-dose ICS/LABA with the same medium-dose ICS alone. Use the full treatment period. RR < 1 favours ICS/LABA. For multi-arm trials, ignore ineligible arms and use the full reported control size and events when that control is shared. Prefer intention-to-treat denominators and the definition closest to moderate-or-severe exacerbations; use severe-only counts if combined counts are unavailable.
single_outcome_target: participants with at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation
